# Herdr selection list: show an actionable error when the worklog is not initialised

## Problem statement

When a project's worklog has not been initialised with `wl init` — or an existing
`.worklog/` has no valid marker (`config.yaml` / `initialized`) — the Herdr
`worklog-selection-list` plugin silently renders an empty selection list. The
operator cannot tell "no work items" apart from "worklog not initialised" and
receives no instruction to fix it.

## Users

Herdr users who open the worklog selection-list plugin in a project whose
worklog has not been initialised (a fresh clone, a new project, or a partial
`.worklog/` left behind).

Example user stories:

- *"As a Herdr user opening the worklist in a project without a worklog, I want
  a clear error telling me the worklog is not initialised and to run `wl init`,
  so that I am not left staring at a blank list."*
- *"As a Herdr user who just ran `wl init`, I want the error to disappear on the
  next refresh without restarting the plugin."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — visible, persistent error instead of a silent blank list.** When no
  valid worklog root can be resolved for the pane's CWD, the selection-list TUI
  renders a persistent error line that names the uninitialised worklog (including
  the resolved path) and instructs the operator to run `wl init`. The pane must
  not render an empty list with no explanation. The line is re-rendered every
  frame while the state holds and disappears on a subsequent refresh once a valid
  worklog root is resolved.
- **AC2 — covers both missing and invalid/partial `.worklog/`.** The error is
  shown whenever `resolveWorklogRoot()` returns `undefined`: a missing
  `.worklog/` and an existing but invalid `.worklog/` (for example only
  `worklog.db`, no `config.yaml`/`initialized`). It must not be shown when a
  valid root is resolved.
- **AC3 — canonical `wl init` wording; non-interactive diagnostic preserved.**
  Every user-facing uninitialised message uses the canonical command `wl init`
  (replacing the current `worklog init` text in `uninitializedReport()` and
  `formatWlError()`). The existing stderr diagnostic is retained for
  non-interactive / TUI-unavailable runs, using the same wording.
- **AC4 — testing/validation.** New or updated unit tests cover: (a) the error
  is present in the rendered output when the worklog root is unresolved and
  absent when it is resolved; (b) the explicit `wl init` wording; (c) the
  invalid/partial `.worklog/` case is treated as uninitialised. Tests live in
  `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` and the worklist renderer tests.
- **AC5 — documentation and full suite.** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (which currently
  states the plugin "shows an empty worklist") and any relevant Herdr worklist
  docs are updated to describe the visible error and `wl init` instruction. The
  full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CHANGELOG.md is
  excluded — it is managed by the ship/release pipeline.)

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only change.** Do not change worklog-root resolution semantics
  (`packages/shared/src/worklog-paths.ts`); the fix is how an unresolved/invalid
  root is surfaced.
- **Fail-open preserved.** The plugin must still start and remain usable when no
  worklog root exists; the fix must not throw or exit non-zero.
- **Non-blocking.** The error must not be a modal that prevents quitting (`q`) or
  normal navigation.
- **Reuse existing rendering patterns.** Prefer the existing banner / empty-state
  mechanism and stay within the `rows - 1` pane invariant; introduce no new
  dependency.
- **UK English** and existing code style.

## Existing state

- `configureWorklogTarget()` (`packages/herdr/src/index.settings.ts`) returns
  `undefined` when `resolveWorklogRoot()` finds no valid `.worklog/`.
- `main()` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`) writes `uninitializedReport()` to
  stderr; once the TUI takes over the screen this diagnostic is effectively lost.
- The `fetcher` in `main()` returns `[]` when `!wlRoot`.
- `createListRenderer` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) renders the empty
  `displayRows` as blank rows with no placeholder message.
- `uninitializedReport()` and `formatWlError()` currently say `worklog init`
  (not the canonical `wl init`).
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` documents the current behaviour: "the herdr plugin
  reports the uninitialized state and shows an empty worklist."

## Desired change

Thread an "uninitialised worklog" notice from `main()` into the selection-list
TUI and render it as a persistent error line (including the resolved path and the
`wl init` instruction) whenever the worklog root is unresolved or invalid. Keep
the stderr diagnostic for non-interactive runs, corrected to `wl init`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.settings.ts` — `uninitializedReport()` copy: `worklog init` → `wl init`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `main()` resolves `wlRoot`, passes the uninitialised notice to `runWorklistTui`, and keeps the `fetcher` empty-list fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — add an uninitialised-notice option to `runWorklistTui`, thread it through `render()` into `createListRenderer`/the empty-state rendering.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.args.ts` — `formatWlError()` copy: `worklog init` → `wl init`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — update the `uninitializedReport` assertion and add unresolved/resolved coverage.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.test.ts` — renderer/empty-state tests for notice present/absent.

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B — decompose `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `worklist.ts` split, I want one automated gate that
fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so that every
extraction child can land safely without touching any existing test file and
without a reviewer having to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 require: every production module ≤1,000 lines, an
unchanged public surface at `./worklist.js`, unmodified test files, no new
circular imports, and a single `WorkItemListState` declaration. Nothing in the

already built exactly this machinery for its own split
(`packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` + `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`);
this child reuses it rather than duplicating it.

- **36 consumer files** import from `./worklist.js`/`./worklist`: 2 production

- **66 distinct symbols** are imported across those consumers; the other 23 of
  the 89 current exports are unused outside the module and become internal
  (parent AC2).
- `WorkItemListState` is declared **once** (`worklist.ts:490`) — the single
  owner AC5 protects.
- `runWorklistTui` is declared once (`worklist.ts:5581`, `export async function`)
  and must stay at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical signature

- The live static import graph already contains one large component that
  includes `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
  (`CYCLE_BASELINE` in `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`). It is
  pre-existing and out of scope; what the gate forbids is a **new** cycle member
  or a new **runtime** cycle (parent AC4).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New **additive** test file `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts`
   (vitest) exists and passes on the current tree **before any production code
   moves**; no existing test file is modified (parent AC3).
2. Committed baseline `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` records
   the 66 consumer-imported symbol names plus provenance (generation command,
   source commit, timestamp, scanned globs).
3. **Public-surface gate:** every baseline symbol is still exported by
   `./worklist.js` (value or type), and every symbol the live consumers import
   from the barrel is exported by it — so a lost or trimmed re-export fails the
   suite (parent AC2).
4. **Single state-owner gate:** exactly one production
   `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module declares `WorkItemListState`

5. **Barrel/cycle gate:** no production `worklist.*.ts` module contains a
   runtime (value) import of `./worklist.js` (nor of `./index.js`); the static
   import graph of `worklist*.ts` modules contains no cycle outside the recorded
   baseline allowlist (parent AC4).
6. **Size gate:** every production `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module is
   ≤1,000 lines, excluding an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains
   only `'worklist.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever
   shrinks (it must remain a subset of the plan-time list). The final barrel
   child empties it (parent AC1).
7. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a duplicated
   `WorkItemListState`, a new cycle) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not
   assumed.
8. **Reuse, do not fork, the scanner:** extend
   `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` minimally so the barrel path, the
   module-family matcher and the single-owner declaration name are injectable
   (each defaulting to today's `downtime-worker` behaviour). The existing
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` and

9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite and the

10. A comment on this item records the baseline generation command and the

1. Parametrise `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`: accept a

# Reduce per-command production startup cost (re-scoped from WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY)

**discovered-from:** WL-0MVHVZMCH0092JCY — Investigate in-process CLI harness cost
**Decision source:** child 1 profile (WL-0MVVXFXM6007QZ2L, commit ebde3586) + child 3 decision gate (WL-0MVVXG4B200968BF).

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want a warm CLI invocation against an already-initialised store
to skip the per-call SQLite schema/migration bootstrap and YAML config re-parse,
so the ~2.2 ms (47 %) of every data-access call that is startup work stops being
paid again on each invocation — in the test suite's ~1200 in-process calls and in
real operator use.

## Context

Measured attribution (`docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` § 'In-process CLI harness
cost', `bench/inproc-harness-profile.json`), median of 5, fresh temp store:

| scenario | total | db open (schema+migrations) | config load | harness-side |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wl list --json` | 4.7 ms | 2.2 ms (47.3 %) | 0.0 ms | 1.5 ms (32.5 %) |
| `wl status` | 4.0 ms | 1.8 ms (44.8 %) | 0.2 ms (5.0 %) | 1.0 ms (25.4 %) |
| `wl create` | 5.1 ms | 2.1 ms (42.1 %) | 0.2 ms (3.8 %) | 0.8 ms (16.2 %) |

`getDatabase()` (`src/cli-utils.ts`) calls `loadConfigRelaxed()` — which reads and
`yaml.load`s the config files — and then constructs `WorklogDatabase`
(`src/database.ts` → `packages/shared/src/database.ts`), which builds a
`SqlitePersistentStore` and runs the schema/migration bootstrap on every open.
This is production behaviour (not a test-harness artefact), so the fix belongs in
`src/`/`packages/shared` rather than in `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Opening an already-migrated store at the current schema version does **not**
  re-run the full migration scan on every open: the fast path is detected by a
  cheap schema-version comparison (e.g. `PRAGMA user_version` / a version table),
  and the slow path is still taken for a new, older, or partially-migrated store.
- Config load is not repeated needlessly within one process when the config files
  have not changed (cache keyed on the resolved config file paths plus their
  mtime/size or content hash), and the cache is invalidated when a file changes.
- Behaviour is unchanged: the full test suite passes with the same test counts,
  and schema-creation/migration/integrity tests are green (including downgrade
  and partial-migration cases).
- Median `wl list --json` warm per-call cost against a fresh temp store drops by
  **>= 30 %** versus the child 1 baseline (4.7 ms → <= 3.3 ms), measured on the
  same host as the median of >= 5 runs with load average quoted, using
  `npm run benchmark:inproc-harness -- --runs 5` (a bench script, never an
  ad-hoc vitest invocation).
- `bench/inproc-harness-budget.json` (WL-0MVVXG3UW00250V5) is regenerated for the
  improved numbers and its guard test still passes; the before/after medians and
  the host load are recorded on this item.
- No test-harness workaround is introduced: `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` keeps
  constructing a database per call, so the saving is real production saving.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — store open + schema/migration bootstrap.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `WorklogDatabase` construction/open path.
- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `getDatabase` (calls `loadConfigRelaxed` per call).
- `src/config.ts` — `loadConfig` / `loadConfigRelaxed` YAML parse.
- `bench/inproc-harness-profile.ts`, `bench/inproc-harness-budget.json` — measurement.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — record the before/after numbers.

## Notes

- The migration path must stay obviously correct: a missed migration is data
  corruption, so the fast path must be conservatively gated and covered by tests
  that start from a real older schema.
- Any per-process config cache must be invalidated on file change; tests must
  exercise that invalidation (edit the config between two calls in one process).

# Remove the `do-not-delegate` flag from the worklog system

## Problem statement

The worklog system currently carries a dedicated `do-not-delegate` tag and a first-class `--do-not-delegate` CLI flag, plus a `--force` override on `wl github delegate`. That mechanism predates the use of the `assignee` field as the scheduling-hold signal: a **non-empty `assignee` now means "held / not available for delegation"**, and an empty `assignee` means the item may be delegated. Keeping both mechanisms means two sources of truth for the same decision, duplicated documentation, a stale TUI/CLI surface, and a tag that every project's automation must special-case.

This item removes the redundant `do-not-delegate` flag and tag guard rail and makes the `assignee` field the single source of truth for delegate eligibility.

## Users

- **Automated dispatchers / schedulers** (for example the herdr downtime worker):
  *As a dispatcher, I want one unambiguous hold signal (`assignee`) so I never have to know whether an item is held by a tag, an assignee, or both, and my selection logic matches the delegate command's logic.*
- **Operators:**
  *As an operator, I want to set or release a delegation hold with the `assignee` field I already use for claims, instead of remembering a second, legacy flag.*
- **Maintainers:**
  *As a maintainer, I want the dead flag, its guard rail, its `--force` escape hatch, its tests and its documentation removed together, so no half-removed surface remains.*

## Rationale (why removal, not deprecation)

- `assignee` already expresses exactly the same intent: `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` and `fetcher.ts` document "a non-empty value is the scheduling hold" and clear it with `--assignee ""` (CAS-guarded with `--if-assignee`).
- The `do-not-delegate` tag is currently duplicated across the tag vocabulary and CLI flags, and must be replicated in every orchestrator (`implement.py`, helper scripts, herdr) to avoid livelocks.
- A tag can be added or removed independently of the claim/hold state, so it can drift out of sync with the assignee. One field cannot drift from itself.

## Desired behaviour

Delegation eligibility is determined solely by `assignee`:

- An item with a **non-empty `assignee`** is **held** and must not be delegated automatically (the delegate command refuses, with a clear message naming the holder).
- An item with an **empty/absent `assignee`** is eligible for delegation.
- Successful delegation continues to set `assignee` to `@github-copilot` (the existing post-assignment state), which naturally holds the item afterwards.
- The `do-not-delegate` tag is no longer written, read, documented or accepted as a CLI option. Any pre-existing `do-not-delegate` tags in stores become inert data and are not migrated automatically (see constraints).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — CLI surface removed.** `wl update` no longer accepts `--do-not-delegate` (option registration, argument normalisation list, and per-id tag mutation removed from `src/commands/update.ts`); `src/cli-types.ts` no longer declares `doNotDelegate`. Invoking the old flag fails as an unknown option rather than silently mutating tags.
- [ ] **AC2 — Delegate guard rail replaced.** `src/delegate-helper.ts` no longer inspects `item.tags` for `do-not-delegate`. Instead it refuses delegation when `item.assignee` is a non-empty string, returning a distinct error key (e.g. `held-by-assignee` / `assigned`) and a human-readable message that names the current assignee and explains that a non-empty assignee is the scheduling hold. `DelegateOptions.force` and the associated force-override warning are removed; the step-by-step docstring is updated.
- [ ] **AC3 — `--force` removed from `wl github delegate`.** `src/commands/github.ts` drops the `--force` option, stops passing `force` to `delegateWorkItem`, and maps the new held-by-assignee error to a clear CLI error (no `--force` hint). The existing interactive open-children confirmation is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC4 — Empty/absent assignee remains delegate-eligible.** Delegation still succeeds for an item with `assignee` unset or `""`, preserving the current happy path and the `assignee: '@github-copilot'` update after a successful assignment.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests updated.** Delete `tests/cli/update-do-not-delegate.test.ts`; remove the `do-not-delegate` cases from `tests/cli/update-batch.test.ts`; rewrite the `do-not-delegate` cases in `tests/cli/delegate-guard-rails.test.ts` as assignee-hold cases (held item refuses, empty/unset assignee proceeds, message names the holder); remove the `doNotDelegate` fake-CLI handling and `Boolean(item.doNotDelegate ?? false)` field from `tests/test-utils.ts`; update the test index in `tests/README.md`. Add/extend a regression test proving the tag is inert (an item still carrying `do-not-delegate` but with an empty assignee delegates normally).
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated.** Remove the `--do-not-delegate` update examples/description and the `--force` delegate option from `CLI.md`; replace them with assignee-based guidance ("set `--assignee <holder>` to hold; clear with `--assignee ""` to release"). Update any delegate documentation that mentions the tag. No remaining user-facing reference to `do-not-delegate` in `CLI.md`, `README.md`, `tests/README.md`, or command help text.
- [ ] **AC7 — No behavioural regression elsewhere.** `assignee` CAS/claim semantics (`--if-assignee`, `--assignee ""`), successful-delegation state, and all other delegate guard rails (open-child warning, push/assign failure handling) are unchanged. Existing suite remains green.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite passes** and `npm run build` (or the project's documented build) succeeds.

## Constraints

- **Single source of truth.** Do not introduce a replacement tag or a migration that rewrites existing `do-not-delegate` tags into assignees automatically; per-project data migration, if desired, is a separate operator action.
- **Assignees set by other agents are holds.** Do not attempt to distinguish "producer hold" from "agent claim" in the delegate guard: any non-empty assignee means held.
- **No widening to herdr/implement.py.** This item removes the flag from the worklog system (CLI, helper, docs, tests). Updates to any consumer (`implement.py`, herdr, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`) that special-cases the tag are follow-ups and should be recorded, not folded in, unless they are required to keep the build green.
- **Backward compatibility:** removing a CLI option is an intentional breaking change. Call it out in the changelog/release note.
- **Preserve the open-children warning** and all non-`do-not-delegate` delegate behaviour exactly.

## Key files (verified in this checkout)

- `src/cli-types.ts` — `doNotDelegate?: string` declaration (~lines 109-110).
- `src/delegate-helper.ts` — `DelegateOptions.force` (~line 33), flow docstring (step 2, ~line 77), guard-rail block (~lines 114-127).
- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--do-not-delegate` option (~line 49), normalisation lists (~lines 58, 65), parsing (~lines 212-219), per-id tag mutation (~lines 482-499).
- `src/commands/github.ts` — delegate `--force` option (~line 767), `force` passthrough (~line 825), error mapping (~lines 847-855).
- `tests/cli/update-do-not-delegate.test.ts` — delete.
- `tests/cli/update-batch.test.ts` — cases ~lines 470-500.
- `tests/cli/delegate-guard-rails.test.ts` — header comment and cases ~lines 276-290.
- `tests/test-utils.ts` — `doNotDelegate` field (~line 241) and fake-CLI reference (~line 407).
- `tests/README.md` — entries at lines 92 and 120.
- `CLI.md` — lines 286, 321-325, 1197.
- Generated `dist/` and `package/dist/` outputs — regenerated by the build, not hand-edited.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** a non-empty `assignee` is already the intended delegation-hold signal in every consumer; confirmed in `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` (~lines 193-209) and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (~lines 305-309).
- **Risk (silent eligibility):** items currently protected only by a `do-not-delegate` tag will become delegate-eligible if their assignee is empty. Mitigation: the replacement guard is tested, and the removal is documented in the changelog as a breaking change so operators can audit tagged items first.
- **Risk (automation drift):** an external orchestrator may still pass `--do-not-delegate`; removing the option makes that fail loudly (which is the desired signal) rather than silently ignoring the hold.
- **Risk (partial removal):** generated `dist/` artifacts could keep exposing the old flag if the build is skipped; AC8 requires a build and AC1/AC3 verify the CLI surface.
- **No schema change:** `do-not-delegate` lives only in the free-form `tags` array; there is no DB column or migration to remove.

## Related / follow-up work

- Consumer cleanup (record as follow-ups if needed): `implement.py`'s `do-not-delegate` selection guard and `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` references, once they exist on `dev`.
- Store hygiene: an operator may optionally strip the now-inert tag from existing items (`wl update <id> --tags ...`), but that is not part of this item.

## Appendix: verification performed while writing this item

- `grep -rn "do-not-delegate\|doNotDelegate" src/ tests/ --include="*.ts"` → `src/cli-types.ts`, `src/delegate-helper.ts`, `src/commands/update.ts`, `src/commands/github.ts`, and the three test files plus `tests/test-utils.ts`.
- `grep -rn "do-not-delegate" --include="*.md"` (excluding `node_modules`/`dist`) → `CLI.md`, `tests/README.md`.
- `packages/tui` and `packages/herdr` contain no `do-not-delegate`/`doNotDelegate` implementation (the README line about a TUI `g` delegate shortcut is stale; no TUI delegate code references the tag).
- `delegateWorkItem` sets `assignee: '@github-copilot'` on success, confirming assignee is the post-delegation hold.

# Goal

As an agent or operator performing worklog housekeeping, I want `wl delete` to accept
`--deleted-by` and `--delete-reason`, so that a soft-delete records *why* the item was removed in the
same command that removes it — instead of requiring a second `wl update` correction pass that is easy
to forget.

Discovered during: WL-0MVYEQKAM003THSP housekeeping (2026-11-02) — the machine-specific epic sweep
needed a non-default reason, and the CLI could not express it.

# Problem

`wl delete` hardcodes both attribution values:

```ts
// src/commands/delete.ts:81-82
const deletedBy = await getConfiguredUserEmail();
const deleteReason = 'deleted via wl delete';
```

`deleteReason` is therefore **not expressible from the CLI at all** — every CLI soft-delete claims
"deleted via wl delete" regardless of intent. `deletedBy` is only ever the configured git identity.

Three concrete consequences:

1. **Intent is lost.** A housekeeping sweep (duplicate, superseded, machine-specific, wrong project)
   is indistinguishable after the fact from an accidental delete. `deleteReason` is persisted on the
   item, synced, and is the field a post-mortem reads — so the loss is permanent and shared with every
   collaborator.
2. **The workaround is two commands and silently skippable.** The only way to set a real reason today
   is `wl delete <id>` followed by `wl update <id> --delete-reason "..."`. That second step is legal
   because the soft-delete guard (`src/commands/update.ts`) permits changes to `deletedBy` /
   `deleteReason` on an already-deleted item — but it is undiscoverable, and skipping it leaves the
   wrong reason recorded with no error.
3. **CLI/API divergence.** The REST API already supports exactly this —
   `src/api.ts` reads `deletedBy` and `deleteReason` from query parameters, defaulting to
   `'deleted via API'` (added by WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO F4). The CLI, which is the primary interface for
   agents, lacks the equivalent.

Attribution is also load-bearing for replication, not just for humans: per the delete command's own
comment, the merge layer's delete-side protection **only propagates attributed deletes** over a live
remote item — an unattributed delete silently fails to propagate. So the flags must never be able to
produce a blank `deletedBy` by accident.

# Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 — Both flags record verbatim.** `wl delete <id> --deleted-by "agent-x" --delete-reason "duplicate of WL-XXXX"`
      persists exactly those values on the item (verified via `--json` output and a subsequent
      `wl show <id> --json`).
- [ ] **AC-2 — Recursive delete propagates attribution.** With `--deleted-by`/`--delete-reason` and a
      parent that has descendants, the target **and every descendant** carry the supplied values (a
      descendant asserting the legacy default instead is a failure).
- [ ] **AC-3 — Defaults unchanged when the flags are omitted.** Omitting both preserves today's
      behaviour exactly: `deleteReason` = `deleted via wl delete`, `deletedBy` = configured git
      identity. Pinned by a test so existing callers (and their assertions) cannot regress.
- [ ] **AC-4 — Attribution can never be silently lost.** An empty or whitespace-only `--deleted-by`
      must either fall back to the configured git identity or fail with a clear, non-zero-exit error
      naming the problem — it must **not** write a blank `deletedBy`, which would produce a delete that
      cannot propagate through merge. Pinned by a test for both `--deleted-by ""` and `--deleted-by "   "`.
- [ ] **AC-5 — No breaking change to the JSON/batch contract.** The per-id `results` array, the
      `deleted`/`failed` summary, the legacy single-id fields and the skip semantics for duplicate or
      descendant ids are unchanged; the flags are purely additive. Existing delete suites
      (`tests/cli/delete-batch.test.ts`, `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts`) pass unmodified.
- [ ] **AC-6 — Surface and docs updated.** `wl delete --help` documents both flags (including the
      default values and the AC-4 fallback); `DeleteOptions` in `src/cli-types.ts` gains both optional
      fields; the soft-delete section of `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (which states `deletedBy` is
      "set by `wl delete`") notes that the CLI can now set attribution explicitly, matching the REST
      API.

# Key Files

- `src/commands/delete.ts` — the hardcoded `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` at lines 81-82; the `.option()` declarations; the JSON `results` builder.
- `src/cli-types.ts` — `DeleteOptions` (line ~201): add `deletedBy?: string` and `deleteReason?: string`.
- `tests/cli/delete-batch.test.ts` — the natural home for AC-1/2/3/5 coverage (in-process CLI harness, real DB mutations).
- `tests/cli/delete-auto-sync.test.ts` — ensure the new flags do not affect the auto-sync invocation contract.
- `src/api.ts` — REST parity reference (lines ~208 and ~430) for naming, defaults and the `|| fallback` shape to mirror.
- `src/commands/update.ts` — the soft-delete guard that currently makes the two-step workaround legal; its comments document the attribution/merge rule behind AC-4.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — soft-delete exclusion section (~line 2305) referencing `deletedBy` set by `wl delete`.

# Non-goals

- Changing `wl delete`'s recursion, sync, batch or skip semantics.
- Adding a prompt/interactive confirmation for the reason — flags only.
- Changing the REST API's existing `deleted via API` default.
- Retrofitting reasons onto already-deleted items (a separate, opt-in cleanup if ever wanted).

# Notes

- Suggested defaults: `--delete-reason` default stays `deleted via wl delete`; `--deleted-by` default
  stays the configured git identity, with the supplied value taking precedence (`options.deletedBy || await getConfiguredUserEmail() || ''`),
  mirroring `src/api.ts`.
- Alternatively `--deleted-by` could be *rejected* when blank rather than falling back; either satisfies
  AC-4, but the fall-back variant matches the API and is less disruptive to scripts that pass an empty
  variable.
data.title: wl delete: add --deleted-by and --delete-reason flags (CLI parity with REST API attribution)

# Parse the proxy's slots_detail_stale and slot_counts_stale flags

## Problem statement

`parseLlamaStatus` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.poller.ts`) reads only
one staleness flag — `slots_stale` — from `GET {proxyUrl}/llama/local/status`.
The proxy serves **three** independent staleness flags, and the two the worker
ignores are the ones that say *which part* of the payload is untrustworthy:

| Proxy field | Meaning | Parsed today |
|---|---|---|
| `slots_stale` | the per-slot detail cannot be paired with the counts | yes → `usablePerSlotSlots()` fails closed |
| `slots_detail_stale` | the detail itself is a last-known snapshot | **no** |
| `slot_counts_stale` | the counts (`available_slots`/`total_slots`) are last-known | **no** |

Consequence: herdr collapses three distinct proxy degradations into one opaque
`slots-unavailable` refusal, so the decision log cannot distinguish "the proxy's
`/slots` query is failing" from "only the counts are cached while the detail is
fresh". During the 2026-11-04 overnight outage the proxy served
`slots_stale: true` together with `slots_detail_stale: true` and
`slot_counts_stale: false` (detail stale, counts fresh) for eight hours — an
8-hour-old frozen snapshot
(`slots_snapshot_age_seconds≈29,057`, `slots_snapshot_source=snapshot`,
`slot_id=unknown`, `measured_cache=0` in the proxy log) — and none of that
distinction reached the decision log or the herdr header.

Similarly `local_abandoned_slots` (served as `2` in that incident, while both
cached slots were frozen `is_processing: true, abandoned: true`) is unparsed, so
the evidence that the snapshot was internally contradictory never reached the
decision entry.

## Goal

A capacity refusal caused by untrustworthy slot data is *attributable* from the
decision log and header alone: the record says which signal was stale, without
reading the proxy's own log on another host.

User story: "As an on-call maintainer triaging a 'nothing dispatched' night, I
want the decision entry to tell me whether the counts, the per-slot detail, or
both were cached, so I can tell a proxy-side observability failure from genuine
GPU saturation."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Both flags are parsed.** `parseLlamaStatus` parses `slots_detail_stale` and
   `slot_counts_stale` with the same optional-boolean contract already used for
   `slots_stale`: absent → `undefined` (pre-feature proxy, behaviour unchanged);
   non-boolean → reject the poll (fail-closed, ambiguous); present → carried on
   `LlamaStatus`.
2. **Refusals stay fail-closed.** Availability is unchanged: `slots` usable only
   when non-empty **and** not `slots_stale`; the count-based fallback stays
   removed. The new flags are evidence, never an alternative budget.
3. **Attribution reaches the decision log.** Every `slots-unavailable` decision
   entry carries the observed flags as additive fields (for example
   `slotsDetailStale`, `slotCountsStale`), following the existing additive
   evidence convention (`auditBatchDepth`, reservation evidence). Entries keep
   their shape when the proxy is pre-feature.
4. **Header token distinguishes, or documents why not.** Either the herdr header
   blocking token distinguishes the stale-detail case from a plain unusable
   payload, or the item records why a single token is retained (with the reason
   in the code comment and the docs).
5. **`local_abandoned_slots` is carried as advisory evidence** on the decision
   entry, so a self-contradictory proxy snapshot (counts say free, detail says
   all slots busy/abandoned) is visible in the record.
6. **Contradictory payload is covered by a test.** A payload with
   `available_slots > 0`, `capacity_hint: "idle"` and all cached slots
   `is_processing: true` never admits a dispatch and records the new evidence
   fields.
7. **Docs updated.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (fail-closed contract /
   decision-log schema) lists the new fields and what each flag means for
   diagnosis.
8. **Full project test suite passes** (`/skill:test`).

## Plan

1. Extend the optional-boolean parsing (reuse the `slots_stale` shape) and add
   the fields to `LlamaStatus`; unit tests for absent / valid / malformed.
   → verify: `downtime-worker.test.ts` parser table extended and green.
2. Thread the flags into `capacityEvidence`/`recordDecision` for the
   `slots-unavailable` path (and `capacity-saturated` where relevant).
   → verify: `downtime-worker.leaf-audit.test.ts` / orchestration tests assert
   the fields on the emitted entry.
3. Cover the contradictory-payload case end-to-end; no dispatch, evidence
   recorded.
   → verify: new test failing before the change, green after.
4. Update the docs schema table and the fail-closed section.
   → verify: docs test / manual check, then `/skill:test` full.

## Key files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.poller.ts` (`parseLlamaStatus`, optional
  boolean helpers).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` (`LlamaStatus`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.ts` (`usablePerSlotSlots`, unchanged
  semantics — availability must not broaden).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` (`capacityEvidence`,
  decision header tokens).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts` (`slots-unavailable`
  refusals).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

## Risks & notes

- **Do not relax the fail-closed contract.** The temptation is to treat "counts
  fresh, detail stale" as a usable signal. It is not: an 8-hour-old detail with
  a fresh count is exactly what starved dispatch for a night. Evidence only.
- **Malformed-flag strictness.** The existing contract rejects the whole poll on
  a malformed availability-affecting flag. Keep that for these two flags, and
  note the drift risk with the proxy team (the proxy has previously emitted
  "not computable" nulls for advisory fields; availability-affecting counters
  must stay numeric).
- **Additive-only log shape.** Decision entries must remain backward compatible
  for existing readers and for `hourlyReasonTally`.

## Related

- RCA: overnight zero-dispatch incident, 2026-11-03T20:51Z → 2026-11-04T08:30Z;
  proxy served a frozen 8-hour slot snapshot (`slots_stale`,
  `slots_detail_stale`) and herdr failed closed with `slots-unavailable`.
- WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW — fail-closed `slots-unavailable` contract (this item adds
  attribution only).
- LP-0MUFSVXID0039ZAQ — llm-manager proxy-side improvement (serve fresh per-slot
  detail; the upstream defect is tracked and being fixed there).
- WL-0MVKNC2N50025HXE — capacity-starvation / long-running pane observation.

## Why

This project's worklog database is behind the installed `wl` version. Every `wl` invocation prints:

```
Worklog: database at /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog/worklog.db has schemaVersion=8 but the application expects schemaVersion=9. Required columns were repaired automatically. see 'wl doctor upgrade' to list and apply pending migrations
```

Required columns are being patched on every invocation instead of migrated, and the git hooks are stale. Discovered during the 2026-11-04 downtime-dispatcher RCA (the same finding exists across the other worklog roots).

## Pending work (from `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json`)

### Schema migrations (0)

_None — only hooks below are pending._

### Outdated git hooks

- pre-push

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want this project's worklog schema and git hooks fully up to date, so that `wl` stops auto-patching columns on every call and so every worklog hook behaves like the current template.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` afterwards reports `pending: []` and no hook whose `status` is not `up-to-date`.
2. `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` was executed against this project's database and applied the migrations listed above.
3. A plain `wl list --json` invocation no longer prints the `schemaVersion=8 … expects schemaVersion=9` warning.
4. **Data-safety check.** The count of items with `needsProducerReview == true` is identical before and after:
   `wl list --json | jq '[.workItems[] | select(.needsProducerReview == true)] | length'`
   Record both numbers on this item.
5. `wl doctor` reports no new findings attributable to this upgrade (any residual finding is recorded on a follow-up item, not ignored).
6. The before/after `--dry-run --json` output is recorded in a comment on this item.

## Plan

1. Capture the baseline: `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` plus the `needsProducerReview` count → comment on this item.
2. Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm`.
3. Re-run `--dry-run` (expect nothing pending) and re-check the `needsProducerReview` count (must be unchanged).
4. If the upgrade touched tracked files (`.githooks/`, hook templates), commit them following build → test → commit order.

## Risks & notes

- `--confirm` applies migrations **non-interactively, including UNSAFE ones**. Review the `[UNSAFE]` entries above before running. The database is the runtime source of truth (SQLite); never edit `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and never run `wl import` (destructive).
- If the `needsProducerReview` count changes, STOP, restore, and raise a `bug` against ContextHub's `wl` migration set instead of continuing — the drop/re-add cycle is the suspected cause of the permanent schema-8 oscillation.

Created from the 2026-11-04 overnight zero-dispatch RCA. Pi session `herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004`, log `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-ContextHub--/2026-11-04T07-55-10-163Z_herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004.jsonl`.

# Standup more focused on user experience

## Problem statement

The daily standup report is currently a dry, flat bullet list of work items
("things done" + technical summaries), which is hard to read aloud and does
not convey what the user gained from the work. The output should be grouped
into meaningful categories, with each completed item described as a
single sentence about its impact on the user experience — without work item
IDs.

## Users

- The operator, who reads/listens to the daily standup (TTS) and wants a
  readable narrative of what changed and why it matters to the user.
- Agent sessions that generate standups and need clear, stable instructions
  for turning the script's structured data into the grouped report.

Example user stories:
- "As the operator, I want the standup grouped by areas such as 'User
  experience when doing Foo' and 'Back end stability under heavy load', so I
  can quickly grasp where progress happened and what each change means for
  users."
- "As the operator, I want each completed item described as one
  user-experience impact sentence without IDs, e.g. 'Improved the speed of
  user interactions with Foo by providing a one-click setup of the deck'."

## Desired change

1. **Categories** are chosen by the LLM (the invoking agent) at report time;
   labels are free-form (e.g. "User experience when doing Foo", "UI layout to
   improve access to key information"). No fixed taxonomy.
2. **Per-item impact sentences** come from a new explicit `## Impact` line in
   the work item description, written by the agent completing the work. Items
   without one (including all existing legacy items, which are **not**
   retrofitted) fall back to the current `Title — user story` phrasing.
3. **Grouped-paragraph format in every section** — "Yesterday I completed work
   on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus items for today",
   "Regressions" and "Blockers" — each section grouped **independently**
   (categories are chosen per section, not per whole report).
4. The deterministic script (`generate_standup.py`) continues to fetch and
   compute the selection data; it also extracts each item's `## Impact`
   sentence into the structured output. The LLM (agent session) does the
   clustering and paragraph rendering, keeping the script testable and the
   agent output interpretable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `generate_standup.py` extracts the `## Impact` sentence from each item's
   description into a dedicated structured field (e.g. `impact`), available in
   `--json` output; a missing/malformed Impact section yields an empty field
   without error.
2. The rendered report is readable as a narrative: it organises each section's

## Goal

As an implement-skill user, I want (a) `run_tests.py --scope changed` to select the tests that actually exercise an edited source module, and (b) a fresh worktree's `packages/shared` to be built (or otherwise resolvable) so TypeScript suites import cleanly, so the changed-scope gate is meaningful and never blocked by a missing build artefact.

Discovered-from: WL-0MW0JF5YE008LV1R (extract github-sync types).

## Observed (WL-0MW0JF5YE008LV1R session, 2026-11-05)

1. **Selection gap.** The session edited `src/github-sync.ts` and added `tests/github-sync/types-module.test.ts`. `run_tests.py --scope changed` selected only the new test file:

   ```
   commands: ['node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/github-sync/types-module.test.ts']
   reason: selected 1 affected test file(s)
   ```

   Ten test files import `../src/github-sync.js` (`github-sync-output`, `github-sync-comments`, `github-import-label-resolution`, `github-sync-progress`, …) and the AST/behaviour guard `tests/github-sync/split-guard.test.ts` reads the barrel from disk. None were selected, so the changed-scope gate validated a single trivial new test while the real regression surface went unchecked (it only ran at the dev-push full-suite gate).

2. **Missing shared build artefact.** The worktree's `node_modules/@worklog/shared` correctly resolves to the worktree's own `packages/shared`, but that tree had **no `dist/`**, so every suite importing the package failed at import time:

   ```
   Error: Cannot find package '@worklog/shared/worklog-paths' imported from '.../src/worklog-paths.ts'
   ```

   Nine of ten selected test files failed for this reason until `packages/shared` was built manually in the worktree (`cd packages/shared && ../../node_modules/.bin/tsc`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A changed-scope run for an edit to `src/github-sync.ts` selects the test files that import it (documented reproduction: the WL-0MW0JF5YE008LV1R change set), or the selection reason names why mapping was impossible.
2. A freshly created worktree can run the TypeScript suites without a manual `packages/shared` build: either `implement.py start` builds it, or resolution falls back to a built copy, and the failure is reported rather than surfacing as N import errors.
3. Regression tests cover both behaviours.

# Regression tests: full-suite verification runs in a pinned isolated worktree

## Problem Statement

`implement.py finish` fast-forwards the main checkout's local `dev` (Step 6,
`git merge --ff-only`) while sibling full-suite runs executed from the main
checkout (audit F3 cache-miss auto-execution and post-push verification) read a
moving working tree — tests from commit X, source from commit Y — producing
phantom failures (WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET).

## Goal (User Story)

As a test-infrastructure engineer, I want regression tests that pin the
mitigation (full-suite runs execute in an isolated worktree against a pinned
commit, and the cache entry is grafted into the main checkout) so the race can
never silently regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Tests covering the mitigation:** tests are added or updated covering the
   mitigation (an isolated-worktree verification run that does not read a
   moving working tree), and the full project test suite passes with the
   change.
2. A test pins that a full-suite run initiated from the main checkout (the
   post-push verification / audit F3 execution path) executes against an
   isolated worktree resolved to a pinned commit — never against the live main
   checkout working tree that a sibling `finish` can fast-forward mid-run.
3. A test pins that the fresh full-suite cache entry produced by the
   isolated-worktree run is grafted into the main checkout's `.worklog/cache`
   (readable by subsequent read-only post-push verification / audit reads) and
   that `mirror_suite_cache` semantics (never overwrite an existing entry) are
   preserved.
4. A test pins that a mid-run fast-forward of the main checkout's local `dev`
   during a suite run (the `state_changed_during_run` quarantine path,
   SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE) never yields a phantom green/red verdict for a
   different tree.
5. A test covers the audit F3 cache-miss auto-execution path: on a cache miss
   the suite is auto-executed in an isolated worktree, not in the audited
   main checkout.
6. All tests are meaningful (assert observable behaviour via public APIs; no
   source-grepping or zero-assertion tests).

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — the suite runner (framework repo, SorraAgents)
- `skill/test_cache.py` — cache + `state_changed_during_run` detection

# Redirect post-push verification full-suite runs to a pinned isolated worktree

## Problem Statement

A full-suite run executed from the main checkout during post-push verification
can race with a sibling `implement.py finish` fast-forwarding the main
checkout's local `dev` (`git merge --ff-only`), swapping source files mid-run
and producing phantom failures (WL-0MVSLXT79008D4X6 evidence: 4 failures in
`tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts` / `tests/herdr/settings.test.ts` at
1abe9618; identical tree green in an isolated worktree minutes earlier).

## Goal (User Story)

As an AI agent running `implement.py finish`, I want post-push verification and
audit cache-miss full-suite runs to execute in an isolated worktree pinned to
the pushed commit — never live in the main checkout — so a sibling finish
fast-forwarding `dev` cannot swap the files a suite is reading.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mitigate the race:** the post-push verification path is updated so that
   full-suite runs execute in an isolated worktree against a pinned commit,
   and the cache entry is grafted into the main checkout — not run live in
   the main checkout where a sibling finish can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.
2. The post-push verification path (and the audit skill F3 cache-miss
   auto-execution path) resolves an isolated worktree for the commit being
   verified and executes the full suite there — not in the live main checkout
   where a sibling `finish` can fast-forward `dev` mid-run.
3. The fresh cache entry produced by the isolated-worktree run is grafted into
   the main checkout's `.worklog/cache` before/mirroring the pre-push hook's
   `mirror_suite_cache` semantics (never overwrites an existing entry), so
   read-only post-push verification and audits serve the grafted entry.
4. The mitigation is minimal and localised: document + redirect test execution
   to worktrees; it does not rewrite the post-push verification pipeline or
   change verdict semantics (`green`/`red`/`missing`/`not_applicable`).
5. The single-owner main-checkout flock lock (WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84) and the
   main-checkout guard (WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O) remain intact; finish refuses
   loudly rather than masking a real failure.

## Problem Statement

When the main checkout's `dev` is fast-forwarded mid-test-run by a sibling
`implement.py finish`, a suite produces failures that exist in **no single
commit** (tests from X, source from Y). The test-failure triage logic can mint
phantom `test-failure` work items from such mixed-tree output, creating noise
and false work for producers (WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET).

## Goal (User Story)

As a producer, I want the triage logic to detect and suppress known phantom
patterns (mixed-tree verdicts from a moving checkout) so they no longer
auto-mint critical `test-failure` work items, while genuine failures still
triage normally.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No phantom test-failure items:** after the mitigation, the race no longer
   generates additional phantom test-failure work items without manual triage;
   existing test-failure triage logic detects and suppresses known phantom
   patterns.
2. The test-failure triage helper detects known phantom signatures — a
   `state_changed_during_run` / mid-run fast-forward flag, or output recorded
   while the executing checkout was not a stable, pinned tree — and suppresses
   auto-creation of a `test-failure` work item, recording the suppression
   reason instead.

   explicit notice (`state_changed_during_run` notice code or equivalent),
   so the information is never silently lost — it is simply not minted as a
   critical item.
4. A genuine failure on a stable checkout still creates/updates a
   `test-failure` work item exactly as before (no behaviour change for real
   failures).
5. The suppression is covered by tests (both a phantom pattern that is

Additive `downtimeWorklogRoots: string[]` on the herdr settings surface (option O1, producer-confirmed 2026-11-06): registered worklog roots the downtime leader may sweep. Fails safe by construction — empty/absent array preserves today's offer-only + own-backlog behaviour byte-for-byte (AC6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fail-safe: an empty or unresolvable registry leaves today's behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged (only offers + own-backlog) (parent AC6).
- `downtimeWorklogRoots: string[]` is added to `PluginSettings` with default `[]`; absent/empty array leaves the candidate universe exactly `offerList ∪ ownBacklog(opts.cwd)` (AC6).
- Elements are worklog ROOT paths (parent of `.worklog/`), consistent with the coordinator's `worklogRoot` semantics; the array is clamped/bounded with deterministic non-string rejection (clamps.ts pattern).
- Load-time validation requires `<root>/.worklog/worklog.db` presence and realpath-normalises symlink roots; invalid entries fail closed but never crash settings load (assumption A1, brief failure-mode mitigation).
- The resolved registry is exposed on the worker/leader opts surface so the sweep reads it at most once per tick.
- Settings/clamps unit suite (T1) is green and the full project test suite must pass with the new changes (AC11).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `PluginSettings` + load/save round-trip
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.clamps.ts` — length clamp
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — opts surface wiring
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.test.ts` — T1 spec

## Dependencies

Depends on T1 (test-first contract). Prerequisite for I3 (sweep consumes the registry).

## Deliverables

Config surface + validation, green against T1.

# Implement: hasPeerOffer liveness-aware predicate

Parent AC7 (option A, producer-confirmed 2026-11-06): peer offers older than `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS` count as absent peers so the leader is never held back by a dead instance's stale entry. Entry expiry (`pruneStaleEntries`) remains a deliberate no-op.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `hasPeerOffer` is made liveness-aware (rejects entries older than `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS`), and the decision is recorded in code comments and docs; entry expiry remains a no-op (parent AC7).
- `hasPeerOffer(entries, instanceId)` gains additive optional `nowMs`/`staleMs` parameters (default `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS`); an entry whose `lastUpdated` is older than the window is treated as no peer (AC7).
- Both call sites (orchestrator-tick, orchestrator-dispatch) pass their live clock; fresh-entry behaviour is unchanged (no cooldown-cancellation regression).
- `pruneStaleEntries` remains a no-op: returns 0 and never mutates the coordination file.
- The conservative decision rationale (stale = absent peer makes the leader more willing to sweep, never less) is recorded in code comments; heartbeat/peer-liveness broadcasts stay out of scope (scope-creep guard).
- Liveness suite (T2) is green; full project test suite must pass with the new changes (AC11).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — predicate
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-tick.ts` — call site 1
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — call site 2
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts` — T2 spec

## Dependencies

Depends on T2 (test-first contract).

Liveness-aware predicate, green against T2, decision documented.

# Implement: registered-root sweep in coordination leader

Core slice (parent AC1-AC5): when the coordination offer list yields nothing dispatchable, the leader sweeps registered roots (`downtimeWorklogRoots`) in round-robin order using the SAME canonical ranking (`getHerdrListHead`) and the FULL existing sequential gate chain — a registered root with dispatchable work but no running herdr instance becomes reachable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A root with dispatchable work but no running herdr instance is reachable by the leader, and work from it is dispatched. Verified on ContextHub (9 dispatchable items, 0 offers → now dispatchable) (parent AC1).
- A sweep must not bypass any existing safety gate — assignee hold, producer-review, code-freeze, freshness, caps, slot minimums, in-flight, review-queue — gates remain sequential filters (parent AC2).
- The canonical ranking contract is preserved: a sweep is a bounded window over registered roots using the same `getHerdrListHead` path, never a second ranking (parent AC3).
- Fairness: no single root can monopolise the leader (bounded per-root share or round-robin cursor), demonstrated by a multi-root test with two roots each holding dispatchable work (parent AC4).
- Fail-open: an unreadable/missing root in the registry is skipped without a strike, and never crashes the tick (parent AC5).
- Fail-safe: an empty or unresolvable registry leaves today's behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged (only offers + own-backlog) (parent AC6).
- Leader sweeps `downtimeWorklogRoots` in round-robin order (reusing the retired-but-functional `selectLeastRecentlyServed` cursor from `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts`) after the offer scan yields nothing dispatchable (AC1/AC4 fairness).
- The sweep head is read via `getHerdrListHead(root, window)` — the same canonical ranking path, bounded window, never a second ranking (AC3); the `getHerdrListHead` dep seam becomes root-aware (honours cwd via `--worklog-dir` resolution, mirroring `getNextItem`).
- The full sequential filter chain applies per swept root — classify (producer-review/freshness/caps), dispatched markers, attempt budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze, CPU gate, audit slot minimums, review-queue hold, in-flight critical guard — reusing the already root-parameterised seams (cooldownEntriesForRoot/inFlightForRoot/reviewGateForRoot). No gate bypass (AC2).
- Dispatch into the registered root uses the existing `dispatchClaimedTier{cwd: root}` claim path; AC1 verified on ContextHub by read-only observation (assumption A2: no persistent config mutation by the implementation itself).
- Unit tests cover the registered-root sweep (multi-root fairness, fail-open, fail-safe, gate preservation) green against T3; full project test suite must pass with the new changes (AC11).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — sweep path
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — root-generic `computeMostImportantItem`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` — cursor reuse
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getHerdrListHead` root seam
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — T3 spec

## Dependencies

Depends on T3 (test-first contract) and I1 (registry input). Prerequisite for I4 (docs record the final model).

## Deliverables

Vertical sweep slice, green against T3; AC1 ContextHub observation recorded.

# Generalise the host dispatch budget to any work item type

## Problem Statement

The host-wide dispatch budget (`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts`,
parent WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB) only covers two kinds: `implement` and `audit`.
`budget.json` is a fixed two-field shape (`{ "maxImplement": 2, "maxAudit": 1 }`),
the `HostBudgetKind` type is `'implement' | 'audit'`, and the interactive
over-quota dialog (`budgetKindForAgentCommand`) recognises only those two.
Capping `plan`, `intake` or `risk-effort` dispatches is currently impossible —
it was explicitly recorded as out of scope in the v1 contract (F6,
WL-0MVXY10QH0020V7S: "Capping the `plan` / `intake` / `risk-effort` tiers is
likewise out of scope").

Operators want one machine-scoped concurrency governor that can cap any kind
of dispatched work, with the same semantics the implement/audit tiers already
have — and they want it to be a general mechanism, not N special cases.

## Users

- **Operators.** As a herdr operator, I want to set a host-wide concurrency
  cap for any dispatch kind (`implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `intake`,
  `risk-effort`), so that I can bound the machine's agent work-in-flight per
  kind — and leave any kind unlimited by simply not configuring it.
- **Downtime dispatcher.** As the dispatch admission path, I want one generic
  budget check for every kind, so plan/intake/risk-effort dispatches are
  subject to the same host-wide constraints (and the same observability) as
  implement/audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Any kind configurable.** `budget.json` accepts a cap for every dispatch
   kind (`implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort`). A cap set
   for any kind is enforced at admission (refuse when live >= cap) on both
   dispatcher paths (direct and coordination leader), with `0` remaining the
   per-kind kill switch.
2. **Absent = unlimited.** A kind not explicitly present in the budget config
   is **unlimited**: admission never refuses it on budget grounds, it is never
   counted against any cap, and its dispatches are not recorded in the ledger
   (no reserve/release bookkeeping for uncapped kinds). No default cap is
   invented for unconfigured kinds.
3. **Existing budgets preserved.** The default stays `implement: 2`,
   `audit: 1`, and an operator's existing `budget.json` values keep their
   meaning and enforcement (same refusal behaviour, same kill switch) — the
   generalisation must not change or silently drop configured caps.
4. **Counting asymmetry preserved, audit-only.** Only `audit` keeps the
   over-hold semantics: it counts fresh ledger entries with **no** live-pane
   requirement (`freshCount` — slot held from reservation until a release
   point fires or the 2 h stale window). Every **other** kind counts only
   fresh entries whose pane is in the machine-wide live pane list
   (`liveCount`), so its slot frees when the pane leaves the live list.
5. **Legacy code removed (no backward compatibility).** The following are
   deleted, not kept behind compat shims:
   - the retired `active-audit` marker readers (`readActiveAuditMarker`,
     `isHostAuditActive` in `machine-coordination.ts`) and the synthetic
     legacy-marker entry count (`legacyActiveAuditCount` / `reduceMarkerCounts`);
   - the `audit-host-saturated` token special-case at `maxAudit: 1`
     (unified to the single `host-budget-audit` refusal token);
   - the fixed two-kind `HostBudgetKind` type and `DEFAULT_HOST_BUDGET_CONFIG`
     shape; the fixed two-key env overrides (`HERDR_HOST_MAX_IMPLEMENT` /
     `HERDR_HOST_MAX_AUDIT`) are generalised or removed;
   - any F6 doc carve-out text describing plan/intake/risk-effort as out of
     scope.
   A repo-wide scan confirms no references to the removed symbols remain
   (module headers, doc comments and the `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
   contract of record updated to match).
6. **Interactive over-quota gate generalised.** A hand-fired
   `/skill:<kind>` dispatch for any capped kind consults the same ledger/cap
   and prompts on over-quota, exactly as implement/audit do today
   (`budgetKindForAgentCommand` generalised to all kinds).
7. **Observability generalised.** The worklist header counter, stderr skip
   line and decision-log tokens report live/max **per configured kind**
   (any capped kind), never for uncapped kinds; an uncapped kind can never
   produce a budget refusal token.
8. **Tests.** Unit + integration tests cover: capped plan/intake/risk-effort
   admit and refuse at their caps; an uncapped kind always admits and records
   nothing; per-kind kill switch `0`; audit over-hold vs live-pane release
   for all other kinds; refusal tokens unified (no `audit-host-saturated`
   anywhere); legacy-marker references gone; existing implement/audit
   behaviour with the default config unchanged. Full project suite passes.

## Constraints

- Scope: `packages/herdr` only (ledger, admission, interactive gate,
  observability, machine-coordination). No worklog (`wl`) / database scoring
  changes; the dispatcher head remains the sole ranking path.
- `scheduled` prompts are **not** a work-item kind and stay outside the
  budget; the budget covers `DowntimeSkillKind` only.
- The budget remains the **outer** concurrency governor: the inner capacity
  gates (free-slot minimums, local reservation/prefill pacing, contention,
  host-CPU gate) keep their existing order and meaning.
- No `window`/rate-limit field (explicitly still out of scope in v1).

## Existing State

- `HostBudgetKind = 'implement' | 'audit'` (`host-dispatch-budget.ts`),
  `DEFAULT_HOST_BUDGET_CONFIG = { maxImplement: 2, maxAudit: 1 }`, clamps
  `0..HOST_BUDGET_MAX (32)`, env overrides `HERDR_HOST_MAX_IMPLEMENT` /
  `HERDR_HOST_MAX_AUDIT`.
- Counting: implement uses `liveCount` (live-pane), audit uses `freshCount`
  (marker semantics, incl. the synthetic legacy-marker entry).
- Admission in `host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`
  (`admitHostDispatch` / `readAuditBudgetState` / `confirmHostDispatch` /
  `releaseHostDispatch`); interactive gate in
  `host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts`; refuse tokens
  `host-budget-implement` / `host-budget-audit` / `host-budget-unknown` plus
  the `audit-host-saturated` compat token.
- The removal of the legacy `active-audit` readers was already scheduled for
  "the release after the host-wide budget generalisation ships"
  (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, F6 removal schedule) — this item is
  that release.
- `DowntimeSkillKind = 'plan' | 'intake' | 'audit' | 'implement' |
  'risk-effort'`; dispatch-classified kinds today are `audit`, `implement`,
  `plan`, `intake` (intake → plan → implement chain) and `risk-effort`
  (effort/risk evaluation for plan_complete items).

## Desired Change

1. Generalise `HostBudgetKind` to all `DowntimeSkillKind` members; the config
   becomes a map over kinds (absent kind ⇒ uncapped). Keep `implement: 2`,
   `audit: 1` as the defaults for those kinds.
2. Admission becomes one generic path: look up the kind's cap; absent ⇒ admit
   without reservation; present ⇒ the existing live-count admission with the
   audit over-hold exception (`freshCount` for `audit` only).
3. Delete the legacy-marker surface and unify the refusal tokens on
   `host-budget-*`.
4. Extend `budgetKindForAgentCommand` and the over-quota dialog to all kinds.
5. Generalise the observability surfaces (counter, skip line, decision tokens)
   to list every configured kind; uncapped kinds never appear.
6. Update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (module tables, gate table,
   removal schedule, out-of-scope wording) and all affected module doc
   comments.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — kind type, config schema,
  live/fresh counting, reap, kill switch
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — generic admission,
  refusal tokens, audit over-hold
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts` /
  `host-budget-dialog.ts` — over-quota gate + dialog for all kinds
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — remove legacy marker readers
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — generalised counter/skip line
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — refusal-token mapping
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — contract of record update
- Tests: `host-dispatch-budget*.test.ts`, `host-budget-dialog*.test.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`, machine tests

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption (recorded):** "Keep the configured budget for any existing
  items in place" means the default caps (`implement: 2`, `audit: 1`) and any
  operator-written `budget.json` values remain honoured exactly; the
  generalisation may change the on-disk schema but must preserve the effective
  caps and enforcement for `implement` and `audit`.
- **Assumption (recorded):** uncapped kinds bypass the ledger entirely (no
  reserve/release entries) — simplest semantics for "not limited"; the
  pane-close release is idempotent by item id and unaffected for capped kinds.
- Risk: generalising the admission seam touches the dispatch choke point;
  mitigated by keeping the counting asymmetry behaviour-preserving for
  implement/audit and by the test matrix (AC8).
- Risk: observability surfaces must not regress for existing kinds — the
  unified `host-budget-audit` token replaces `audit-host-saturated`, so any
  operator tooling keyed on the old token must be updated in the same change.

## Related Work

- WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB (completed) — parent: host-wide concurrency budget for
  implement and audit dispatches (this item extends it)
- WL-0MVXY0XPF006YUHA (completed) — F2 audit 1→N generalisation + active-audit
  unification, which scheduled the legacy-marker removal this item performs
- WL-0MVXY0WQF0069YDJ / WL-0MVXY0YG7009JMHI / WL-0MVXY0Z93002HKCZ /
  WL-0MVXY0ZYW009NEJD / WL-0MVXY10QH0020V7S / WL-0MVXY11IL0032S07
  (completed) — F1–F7 slices of the original budget work

---
*Created from a user request to extend the budget workflow to any work item
type, with unlimited default for unconfigured kinds, no backward-compatibility
requirement (dead code removal permitted), existing budgets preserved, and the
over-hold approach retained for audit only.*
data.title: Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item type (absent = unlimited, audit-only over-hold)

# herdr extension key chords to set a work item's assignee

Add herdr worklist key chords (same mechanism as the existing `c q` quick-create chord —
`packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` / `loadShortcutConfig`, worklist input loop) that
set the focused work item's assignee to one of the three hold identities, or clear it:

- `a p` — assignee = `producer`
- `a a` — assignee = `agent`
- `a n` — clear the assignee (`--assignee ""`)
- `a d` — assignee = `dispatcher`

## Goal

Give the operator one-key access to the scheduling-hold semantics that drive dispatch:
setting a producer hold, tagging an agent claim, clearing a stale hold, or (after
WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG) marking an item as dispatcher-handled — without hand-editing via CLI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1**: The four chords (`a p` / `a a` / `a n` / `a d`) are registered in the herdr
  shortcut config for the worklist view and work on the focused item.
- **AC2**: Each chord runs `wl update <id> --assignee <value>` (or the equivalent
  worklog-dir-safe update) against the focused item; `a n` clears the assignee.
- **AC3**: The updates flow through the standard command/refresh path (a completion-refresh
  re-renders the worklist, mirroring chord-quick-create).
- **AC4**: Chord conflicts are handled: the second keys (`p`, `a`, `n`, `d`) must not collide
  with existing handlers (quit-key case documented in chord-quick-create).
- **AC5**: The chords are documented in the herdr README / CLI.md keybinding reference, with
  the hold semantics of each identity (`producer` = persistent hold, `agent` = session claim,
  `dispatcher` = non-hold after WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG, empty = dispatchable).
- **AC6**: Unit tests drive the real worklist input loop with the production shortcut registry
  for all four chords (same harness as chord-quick-create.test.ts), asserting the dispatched
  `wl update` command and assignee value.
- **AC7**: Full project test suite passes with the change.

## Notes

- The `dispatcher` identity is a scheduling NON-hold only after WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG lands;
  until then `a d` would create a hold — sequence or gate the chord so it matches the
  dispatcher-claim semantics at the time it is used (document the pre/post state).
- Follow the settings/shortcut validation pattern in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`.

## Related Work

- discovered-from: WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y — Downtime leader cannot see a worklog root with no
  running herdr instance (the stack that exposed how opaque the assignee/hold machine is).
- WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG — Dispatcher claims work items as 'dispatcher' instead of producer
  sentinel 'Map' (critical; defines the `dispatcher` identity this chord writes).
- WL-0MTCLB50D0026YA7 — the `c q` quick-create chord this work mirrors.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — chord registry
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` / `worklist.state.ts` / `worklist.constants.ts` — input
  loop and focused-item resolution
- `packages/herdr/src/chord-quick-create.test.ts` — test harness to mirror
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `CLI.md` — keybinding documentation

The pi startup context budget gate has zero headroom in both repositories: ContextHub AGENTS.md measures 2588 B against a 2588 B threshold, and SorraAgents AGENTS_GLOBAL.md measures 15226 B against a 15226 B threshold. Any documentation addition therefore fails the dev-push gate unless the same file is trimmed elsewhere — a tax that pushed two children of WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG into rewriting unrelated prose to free bytes.

Desired outcome:
- Decide and record the policy: raise the thresholds deliberately (with rationale and measured values), or trim the startup surface so a small addition fits.
- Make the gate's failure message name the file, measured vs allowed bytes, and the fact that a net-negative edit is required.
- Keep the guard meaningful (it exists to stop unbounded startup-context growth).

Add a golden-output test that renders a sample report and asserts grouped sections, no work item IDs, and Impact-first sentences.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Golden-output test renders a sample report from fixed structured data.
2. Asserts grouped section headings are present and well-formed (Yesterday, Open critical items, Additional focus, Regressions, Blockers).
3. Asserts no work item IDs appear anywhere in rendered output (regex check for `WL-...` and ID parentheses).
4. Asserts impact-first sentences are used when `impact` is present, fallback otherwise.
5. Test is hermetic (no network/sync/commit via `--no-sync --no-commit` or injected data).
6. Parent AC — Testing/validation: unit tests cover Impact extraction (present, absent, malformed) and the fallback; a golden-output test renders a sample report and asserts grouped sections, no IDs, and Impact-first sentences.

## Key Files:
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_golden_report.py`

## Dependencies
- Impact-aware report rendering (sibling feature).

# Description

Replace the static Report Structure template in `skill/standup/SKILL.md` with instructions for the invoking agent to cluster each section's items into free-form, LLM-chosen categories and render grouped paragraphs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. SKILL.md instructs the agent to cluster items **independently within each section** (Yesterday, Open critical items, Additional focus, Regressions, Blockers) into free-form category labels chosen at report time (no fixed taxonomy).
2. Instructs one paragraph per category, one impact-focused sentence per item.
3. States the `## Impact` sentence is used when present, else the `Title — user story` fallback.
4. Reiterates no work item IDs anywhere, first-person, TTS-friendly, ~2-minute budget.
5. Keeps the deterministic data-layer contract: script fetches `--json` structured data; agent renders.
6. Any example output in SKILL.md reflects the grouped-paragraph format.
7. Parent AC — The rendered report is readable as a narrative: it organises each section's items into categories chosen by the LLM at report time, items are grouped **independently within each section**, and no work item IDs appear anywhere in the rendered report.

## Key Files:
- `skill/standup/SKILL.md` (SorraAgents repo source of truth)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/SKILL.md` (installed copy)

## Dependencies
- Impact-aware report rendering (sibling).

# Description

Update work-item completion guidance so newly completed items carry an `## Impact` sentence describing the user-experience impact, enabling future standups to have real impact sentences.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Project `AGENTS.md` (ContextHub) completion conventions include the `## Impact` requirement (one sentence, user-experience impact).
2. Global `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` reflecting the same convention where work-item completion is described.
3. Intake brief template / intake skill guidance mentions `## Impact` as an optional-but-recommended description section.
4. Existing completed items are explicitly **not** retrofitted (documented as intentional).
5. Wording is consistent across all touched files and does not conflict with existing conventions.
6. Parent AC — Work-item completion guidance (project AGENTS.md / implement skill / intake brief template) is updated so newly completed items carry an `## Impact` sentence describing the user-experience impact of the change.
